sources.title: Alan Edelman, Tomás A. Arias, and Steven T. Smith, The Geometry of Algorithms with Orthogonality Constraints
sources.locator: Complete 51-page PDF retrieved and extracted. Read §§2.3.2 and 2.5, printed pp. 314–322: Grassmann quotient by frame rotations, projector representation, horizontal tangent directions, gradient and Hessian formulas. The local complex projector chart and sufficient-minimum proof are established independently in this batch.

read_evidence.method: Downloaded the complete PDF to /tmp/pcvar-eas-1998.pdf, extracted all pages with MuPDF to /tmp/pcvar-eas-1998.txt, and read the complete cited sections.

contents.name: §2.3.2, Grassmann points as equivalence classes of orthonormal frames under within-subspace rotations
contents.support: The source identifies the quotient gauge; the local item proves the corresponding unitary-frame equivalence for complex Hermitian projectors.

contents.name: §2.5, unique projector representation and horizontal Grassmann tangent directions
contents.support: The local item derives the complex graph-chart formula and all off-diagonal Hermitian tangent directions directly.

contents.name: §2.5.3–§2.5.4, Grassmann gradient and Hessian formulas
contents.support: The source treats stationarity and second derivatives on the Grassmann manifold; the local commutator and strict-minimum proofs state their own complex hypotheses and derivations.

contents.name: §2.5, projector tangent directions as skew-Hermitian commutators
contents.support: The source treats tangent directions through projector geometry; the local item proves the complex Hermitian commutator representation and constructs a unitary Cayley curve with that velocity.

sources.title: P.-A. Absil, R. Mahony, and R. Sepulchre, Optimization Algorithms on Matrix Manifolds, Chapter 3
sources.locator: Complete 37-page Chapter 3 PDF retrieved and extracted. Read §§3.4.4 and 3.5.7, printed pp. 31–40: Grassmann as a quotient of full-rank frames and tangent vectors to embedded submanifolds.

read_evidence.method: Downloaded the complete chapter to /tmp/pcvar-absil-chap3.pdf, extracted all pages with MuPDF to /tmp/pcvar-absil-chap3.txt, and read the complete cited sections.

contents.name: §3.4.4, Grassmannian as a quotient whose points are subspaces rather than chosen frames
contents.support: The source's real quotient construction motivates the graph chart; the local proof gives the complex Hermitian projector construction explicitly.

contents.name: §3.5.7, tangent vectors to embedded submanifolds arise from differentiable curves
contents.support: The local proof differentiates the projector identities and constructs the converse graph curve, so both tangent inclusions are verified.

contents.name: §3.5.7, tangent directions to the embedded Grassmannian
contents.support: The source supplies the real embedded-manifold tangent viewpoint; the local proof verifies the complex projector tangent set and the commutator curve directly.

sources.title: Eric Cancès and Claude Le Bris, On the convergence of SCF algorithms for the Hartree-Fock equations
sources.locator: Complete 27-page PDF retrieved and extracted. Read §2.1 and Lemmas 1–3 with their proofs, printed pp. 751–755: density-operator projectors, orbital-unitary gauge, the Hartree-Fock energy, and commutation at stationary points. The article explicitly distinguishes finite-dimensional compactness from continuum existence and does not provide a general local-minimum theorem.

read_evidence.method: Downloaded the complete article to /tmp/pcvar-cances-lebris-2000.pdf, extracted all pages with MuPDF to /tmp/pcvar-cances-lebris-2000.txt, and read the complete cited sections and proofs.

contents.name: §2.1, Hartree-Fock density operators are rank-N orthogonal projectors and quotient out orbital-unitary gauge
contents.support: The local definition restricts the physical vocabulary to a supplied finite model and does not claim an exact continuum Hartree-Fock functional.

contents.name: §2.1 and Lemma 2, first variation on the trace-constrained density-operator tangent space
contents.support: The local proof derives the finite-dimensional complex commutator criterion from the explicit graph-chart tangent directions and the Frobenius gradient.

contents.name: §2.1, stated limitations on continuum Hartree-Fock existence and stationary-point structure
contents.support: This batch proves only compact finite-dimensional model existence and explicitly excludes continuum existence or a general stationary-point minimum claim.

sources.title: Daniel Arovas, Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §7.4 Variational Density Matrix Method
sources.locator: Complete chapter page retrieved. Read §7.4, ‘The variational principle’: the density-matrix free energy Tr(ρH)+β⁻¹Tr(ρ log ρ), positivity/normalization constraints, and the variational role of entropy. The fixed-particle fermionic domain and its Fermi-Dirac multiplier are derived locally in this batch.

read_evidence.method: Downloaded the complete 214,748-byte chapter page to /tmp/pcvar-arovas-density-matrix.html, extracted its text to /tmp/pcvar-arovas-density-matrix.txt, and read the complete variational-principle section.

contents.name: §7.4, density-matrix entropy contributes Tr(ρ log ρ) to the finite-temperature free energy
contents.support: The local definition uses the fermionic fixed-particle entropy Tr(D log D+(I-D)log(I-D)) with explicit endpoint conventions.

contents.name: §7.4, varying density-matrix probabilities under a normalization constraint gives thermal occupations
contents.support: The local proof handles the fixed trace constraint, complex Hermitian matrix variations, uniqueness of the chemical potential, and the distinction from nonlinear self-consistency.

sources.title: Christoph Helmberg, Guilherme Porto, Guilherme Torres, and Vilmar Trevisan, An interlacing property of the signless Laplacian of threshold graphs
sources.locator: Complete 14-page PDF inspected. Read §2, Theorem 2, which states the real-symmetric Weyl sum inequalities; the Hermitian perturbation estimate is proved locally by realification.

read_evidence.method: Opened and inspected the complete 14-page arXiv PDF, including §2 and Theorem 2.

contents.name: §2, Theorem 2, Weyl inequalities for real symmetric matrices
contents.support: The local item realifies Hermitian matrices, proves that this preserves operator norm and doubles eigenvalues, then applies the real Weyl inequalities to obtain the complex version needed for entropy continuity.
